Morbi, which produces nearly 90% of India's ceramics and sanitaryware, depends heavily on gas to keep its kilns running 24x7

Any disruption to energy supplies through the gulf puts production, jobs, and supply chains at risk

While the industry has slowly begun to revive after recent challenges, looming geopolitical tensions have kept the uncertainties intact

A recent order by SEBI has found some striking detail on Rajesh Exports, a gems & jewellery firm, that once used to be a Fortune 500 company.

SEBI undertook an investigation on the company for the period between 2020-2024, and found that 99.8% revenue of Rajesh Exports probably doesn't exist.
That amounts to more than ₹15 Lakh Cr. of revenue inflation.

Company has also been alleged to have made many financial misreporting and maintaining non-transparency with the regulator and markets.

The stock of Rajesh Exports has fallen nearly 10% in 2 days since the order came out.

Check out the post to know more!

Is the AI dream coming to an end?

For the last two years, companies have been rushing to plug AI into everything
The goal seemed simple: cut costs and boost productivity

But the bills are starting to pile up
Many companies are reportedly exhausting their annual AI budgets within weeks. Others are discovering that the productivity gains don’t necessarily justify the costs

As questions around ROI grow louder, even companies like Microsoft and Uber are looking closely at how AI is being deployed and where costs can be reduced

Where do we go from here? Thoughts?

China imposed a ban on chips from the US tech giant Nvidia, given that US was allowing only subpar chips to be sold to China

Interestingly, this ban was announced when the US delegation, including Donald Trump and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, was present in China for a high level diplomatic visit

Needless to say, the timing was hard to ignore
